hints.title: Greedy Minimization
hints.text: To give subsequent elements the greatest leeway to be strictly increasing, make each element as small as possible while exceeding the previous value.

hints.title: Prime Precomputation
hints.text: Precompute all prime numbers up to 1000 using a sieve.

hints.title: Largest Subtracted Prime Selection
hints.text: For element x and previous value prev, pick the largest prime p < x such that x - p > prev. If no valid p exists, verify that x > prev.

hints.title: Greedy Prime Subtraction Implementation

complexity.time: O(n * P + M log log M)
variables: P: number of primes up to 1000
complexity.notes: Sieve up to 1000 takes O(M log log M); scanning primes per element takes O(n * P).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Non-greedy choices may leave numbers too large to be followed by strictly increasing values.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(M) space for precomputed prime table.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Greedily minimizes each value using precomputed primes.
